NAME SWEEP LOG — Open Library search-inside, 2026-09-06
=======================================================
p_430 asks for the camp's PEOPLE to be run against the Internet Archive book corpus, and CLAUDE.md's
Phase 2 mandate says to "log every search attempted and its result (even null results) so the same
ground is not re-covered." This file is that log. It is the authoritative record of which names have
been run; if a name is not here, it has not been swept.

Method: bare-name phrase query against https://openlibrary.org/search/inside.json (contract at
f_4933). Where a name returns many hits, they were read far enough to say whose they are.


THE CAMP'S OWN NAME — ALTERNATIVE SPELLINGS
--------------------------------------------
  "Kanawana"        76 items   (swept earlier 2026-09-06; the enumeration is in p_430)
  "Camp Kanawana"    8 items   (the phrase every earlier pass used, and the reason this was late)
  "Kamp Kanawana"   13 items   ** TWO OF THEM IN NEITHER LIST ABOVE ** — the DLB entry on Stuart
                               McLean (f_4949) and the American Camp Association textbook (f_4950)
  "Kanawanna"        0
  "Lac Kanawana"     0
  "Kanawana, Que"    0
  "Lake Kanawana"    1 item    — the Stuart McLean passage already read (f_4941)

CONCLUSION: run BOTH "Kanawana" and "Kamp Kanawana". The other spellings are dead and need not be
run again.

  Johnston W. Abraham ..... 1 hit, AND IT IS AN OPEN LEAD, NOT A FINDING. The Union List of
                            Manuscripts in Canadian Repositories, supplement 1979-1980 (Public
                            Archives Canada, 1982), leaf 288: "... Annual reports, correspondence,
                            membership lists, memorabilia and press clippings. Ref./Réf.: P.A.C.,
                            MG 28 (I 280). Provenance: Johnston W. Abraham, DeWittville, Que."
                            The fonds runs 1917-1978, 10 cm. THE COLLECTION'S NAME WAS NOT
                            RECOVERED: the Union List is set in two columns, the OCR interleaves
                            them, and six attempts to walk backwards to the heading ran into
                            entries for the Sherbrooke and District University Women's Club on both
                            sides. Nor is it established that this is Kanawana's Johnston W. Abraham
                            (Business Manager from about 1914, documented in his ninth year in
                            1922) rather than another man of the same name.
                            WHY IT IS WORTH KEEPING ANYWAY: it is a precise archival reference at
                            Library and Archives Canada — MG 28 (I 280) — which a person with
                            ordinary browser access resolves in one lookup, and this environment
                            cannot, the LAC gateway returning HTTP 403 (see p_428). Tracked there.

                            missed it belongs in the ZEROTH STEP below: THE SCAN'S OCR DOUBLE-SPACES
                            BETWEEN WORDS, so a grep for "FREDERICK H. SPINNEY" with single spaces
                            returns ZERO across all ten volumes while the double-spaced form returns
                            fourteen. Search these texts with [[:space:]]\+ or a bare substring,

THE ZEROTH STEP, RUN PROPERLY — a word-boundary grep of the nine YMCA Year Book volumes now held
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
After the Holliday failure above, every name in this file plus the unswept list below was grepped,
with word boundaries, across the nine volumes of the Year Book and Official Roster this project now
holds (1893, 1894, 1895, 1896, 1897, 1906, 1907, 1908, 1921), and every hit checked for a Montreal
or Quebec context. Result:

  MONTREAL-CONTEXT HITS — two, and both already recorded:
    A. O. Dawson, President of the Montreal association, 1921 volume (and a member of the
      International Committee's own board) — recorded in f_4964, and NOT Ralph H. Dawson.
    H. C. Paterson, Montreal, Westmount, Physical, entered 08 — recorded in f_4964's roster.

  EVERYTHING ELSE IS A NULL, and an informative one. Owens, Shantz, Charlton, Cornell, Seaman,
  Potts, Ellis, Dimock, Abraham, Cowan, Bradford, Turner, Miller, Lummis, Twynam, Langille,
  Macdiarmid, Hanagan, Robitaille and Ereaux appear in these volumes ONLY as other men in other
  cities. (R. L. Charlton's two hits are an English YMCA secretary at "Worcester Copenhagen St" —
  Charlton Jones — in the British section.)

  WHAT THE NULL MEANS. These volumes roster PAID ASSOCIATION OFFICERS. The men absent from them are
  the camp's volunteers, committee members and seasonal staff — which is the same conclusion the
  Spinney and Powter finds produced from the other direction (f_4958, f_4960, f_4966). The Montreal
  YMCA's paid officers are now known for nine years; the camp's own people mostly were not paid
  officers, and will be found in schools, universities and city directories instead.

THREE PIECES OF ADVICE, THE FIRST OF WHICH IS NEW AND COST SOMETHING.

  ZERO. GREP THE CACHE FIRST. `grep -ril "<name>" sources/cache/` takes one command. The Holliday
  entry above is what happens when it is skipped: a full-text index of millions of books returned
  243 hits about the wrong man, and the right one was in this repo. Sixteen of the twenty-four
  names swept so far returned nothing usable from the corpus, and at least one of them was here.
  AND BEFORE ANY OF THAT, READ THIS: THE OPEN LIBRARY SEARCH-INSIDE API PAGES, AND EVERY NAME SWEPT
  THROUGH IT BEFORE 2026-09-06 SAW ONE PAGE. A query reports its total and returns TWENTY hits. The
  parameter is &page=N; &from= and &offset= are accepted and silently ignored. So a name recorded
  here as returning "N hits, none of them him" was checked against at most twenty of them, and a
  name with 243 hits was checked against 8% of them. THE HIGH-COUNT NAMES IN THIS FILE ARE NOT
  SWEPT, THEY ARE SAMPLED — Holliday's 243 Indianapolis hits above are the clearest case, and he
  turned out to be in this repo's own cache all along. Re-run the common names with paging before
  trusting any null recorded here. See f_4998.

  (Word boundaries matter when you do it: "Ereaux" matches "Devereaux" and "Spinney" matches the
  noun "spinneys", both of which produced false hits in the first pass. AND SPACING MATTERS AS MUCH:
  these scans' OCR routinely puts TWO OR MORE SPACES between words, so a full name typed naturally —
  "Frederick H. Spinney" — can return ZERO against a corpus that contains it fourteen times. That is
  exactly what happened to Spinney's first name for a day. Match on the surname alone and read the
  context, or use [[:space:]]\+ between the parts; never grep a multi-word name with single spaces
  and then record the zero as a fact about the world.)

TWO MORE PIECES OF ADVICE FROM THE NAMES ALREADY RUN, THE FIRST OF WHICH WAS WRONG.
[CORRECTED 2026-09-06 by testing it.] This file used to say: 'Names that are common in English
(Crawford, Holliday) return hundreds of hits about other people and should be paired with
"Montreal", "Y.M.C.A." or "Kanawana" from the start.'

PAIRING WITH A CONTEXT WORD DOES NOT DISAMBIGUATE IN THIS API. Multiple quoted phrases are ANDed
ACROSS THE WHOLE ITEM, not required to appear near each other. '"W. J. Holliday" "Montreal"' was
run with paging on 2026-09-06: 134 hits, and every one examined is still the INDIANAPOLIS ART
COLLECTOR AND RARE-BOOK MAN of the earlier sweep — the Indianapolis Museum of Art donor, the
neo-impressionist collection, the Plains-and-Rockies bibliography — with "Montreal" matching
somewhere else entirely in the same volume, usually in a bibliography of Canadiana. The pairing
narrowed 243 hits to 134 and changed nothing about who they are.

SO: pairing with "Kanawana" is worth doing, because the word is rare enough that co-occurrence in
one book means something. Pairing with "Montreal" or "Y.M.C.A." is nearly worthless — both are
common enough to co-occur with anything Canadian. For a common name, the honest options are to
page the whole result set and read it, or to find a source where the man is likely to be indexed
and search THAT, which is what actually worked for Harold C. Cross (the International Council of
Religious Education Yearbooks) and for W. J. Holliday himself (this repo's own cache).

AND THE HOLLIDAY NULL NOW STANDS PROPERLY: the Montreal YMCA's W. J. Holliday is not in this book
corpus under that name. The earlier sweep reached the right conclusion by a method that could not
have supported it; it is now supported. (One caveat on that run: page 4 of 7 returned an empty
body, so 100 of the 134 were collected, not all of them.)

THE SECOND PIECE OF ADVICE STANDS. Names that are rare (Ereaux, Hanagan, Brandon with
initials) return zero, and a zero here is a fact about a book corpus and not about the world — these
men are in city directories, church records and newspapers that the Internet Archive's book
collection does not contain.

AND THE YIELD IS NOT PROPORTIONAL TO THE NAMES. Of the first nine names swept, six returned nothing
usable, one returned an open archival lead, and two opened real biographies — one of which
(Hay Finlay) turned out to answer a standing open question in another article using facts this
project had already had for weeks. There is no way to tell in advance which is which.
